entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Asina (c. 310–259 BCE) was a Roman general and statesman who played a pivotal role in the First Punic War.

  Asina was one of the most prominent Roman generals of his era, serving under the consuls Publius Cornelius Scipio Nasica and Tiberius Sempronius Longus.

  His military campaigns in Sicily and Corsica marked the first major Roman victories in the war, ultimately forcing Carthage to negotiate a peace treaty.

  Asina's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he was also instrumental in shaping Roman politics and governance.

  His contemporaries praised Asina's military prowess and civic virtues, with the Roman historian Polybius noting that he was 'esteemed for his courage and his moderation'.

  To this day, Asina remains a fascinating figure in Roman history, offering valuable insights into the complexities of ancient Roman politics and warfare.
